title: The Farmer Whose Heart Failure Came With a Year-Old Shoulder Injury

sections.heading: The Patient's Story
sections.content: He is 70 years old and farms for a living. Three months before this admission, he developed shortness of breath — initially mild, grade 2, and progressing to grade 3 — along with orthopnea (breathlessness when lying flat). Over the last 10 days he'd also had giddiness immediately on standing, and pedal edema had been building for two months, gradually worsening though it eased somewhat with medication. He also has pain in his right shoulder and elbow going back a year, after being hit with a stick by his son. He has a known history of heart failure, but no diabetes, hypertension, tuberculosis, asthma, or epilepsy. He drinks toddy occasionally.

sections.heading: What the Work-Up Showed So Far
sections.content:
- General exam: conscious, coherent, cooperative
- Vitals: febrile, blood pressure 90/70 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, respiratory rate 16/min, oxygen saturation 97%
- Cardiorespiratory exam: heart sounds normal, bilateral air entry
- Abdominal exam: soft, non-tender
- Neurological exam: normal
- Investigations sent: 2D echocardiogram and ultrasound abdomen, alongside routine blood work

Working diagnosis: heart failure with mid-range ejection fraction, secondary to dilated cardiomyopathy, with rotator cuff tendinitis and secondary osteoarthritis of the right elbow, plus osteoarthritis and synovitis of the right knee.

sections.heading: How the Story Unfolded on the Ward
sections.content:
He was started on furosemide, a proton pump inhibitor, a B-complex injection, strict fluid and salt restriction, ramipril, and aspirin-atorvastatin combination therapy on the day of admission. By day one, a multivitamin was added, and by day two, clopidogrel and isosorbide dinitrate joined his regimen — building out a more complete heart-failure and secondary cardiovascular prevention plan.

Around this time, he reported persistent pain in his right shoulder and elbow, tracing back to the injury from a year earlier. Examination found diffuse tenderness in both joints with painful, restricted range of motion. X-rays of the right shoulder showed sclerosis at the greater tuberosity, and X-rays of the right elbow showed osteophyte formation at the articular margins of the radius and ulna — confirming degenerative joint changes layered onto his old injury, which were incorporated into his final working diagnosis alongside his cardiac picture.
